Moraga.headline: Moraga turns drier this afternoon, then watches a weekend shower return
Moraga.text: Moraga starts Friday with a few lingering showers, but the National Weather Service expects the shower coverage to fade through the afternoon and most of the evening to turn dry. The air mass stays chilly, with another cold start Saturday before a weaker front brings light rain late Saturday into Sunday; regional totals look modest, around a tenth to a quarter inch. Monday is the best dry break. A stronger Tuesday–Wednesday system could bring renewed, heavier rain, so keep drainage areas clear while soils remain wet.

Lafayette.headline: Lafayette gets a cool break before the next Pacific front
Lafayette.text: Lafayette should see any leftover Friday showers taper by early afternoon, followed by a brighter, chilly afternoon and a mostly dry evening. Saturday looks quieter at first, then a weaker front may bring light rain late in the day and into Sunday; the regional Bay Area estimate is roughly a tenth to a quarter inch through early Monday. Monday offers the clearest pause. A stronger system is expected Tuesday into Wednesday, with another round of rain and gusty winds possible, though exact local totals remain uncertain.

Danville.headline: Danville dries out today, but another rain chance arrives Saturday
Danville.text: Danville may catch a few lingering showers Friday morning, but the NWS expects activity to decrease during the afternoon as the cold upper low moves east. Friday evening should be mostly dry and cool. A weaker front reaches the North Bay late Saturday and spreads across the Bay Area later in the day, bringing light, uneven rain into Sunday; Monday is the best break. A stronger Pacific system is forecast Tuesday–Wednesday, with renewed rain and gusty winds possible. Keep an eye on drainage after this week's soaking.

Greenbrook.headline: Danville's Greenbrook area gets a lull before weekend showers
Greenbrook.text: Danville's Greenbrook area should see leftover showers fade Friday morning or early afternoon, then turn brighter and chilly for the evening. Saturday begins quieter, but a weaker front may bring light rain late Saturday and into Sunday; totals across the interior Bay Area are expected to be modest, though a heavier passing shower could briefly pond water. Monday looks like the best dry window. A stronger system approaches Tuesday–Wednesday, bringing another chance of widespread rain and gusty winds. Keep storm drains and low spots clear.

Marin City.headline: Marin City sees showers ease, with king-tide concerns next week
Marin City.text: Marin City should see the last Friday showers taper by early afternoon, followed by a cool, mostly dry evening. A weaker front brings another chance of light rain late Saturday into Sunday, while Monday offers a short break before a stronger Tuesday–Wednesday system targets the North Bay and coastal mountains with higher rainfall potential. Marin County is urging residents to avoid nonessential travel from 9 in the morning to 4 in the afternoon Tuesday through Thanksgiving as king tides peak. Watch low-lying approaches and drainage, especially when rain coincides with high water.

Sausalito.headline: Sausalito's waterfront gets a lull before king tides and more rain
Sausalito.text: Sausalito's NWS point forecast keeps rain mainly before 8 a.m. Friday, then turns brighter with a high near 56°F. Another weak front brings rain late Saturday and Saturday night, with a 50% shower chance Sunday; Monday should be partly sunny with only a slight early rain chance. The bigger concern arrives Tuesday–Wednesday, when a stronger system may bring rain and wind as king tides peak. Marin County advises avoiding nonessential travel from 9 in the morning to 4 in the afternoon Tuesday through Thanksgiving; low waterfront roads may be especially vulnerable.

Brentwood.headline: Brentwood gets a quieter Friday before a wetter holiday week
Brentwood.text: Brentwood should see any leftover showers diminish by early afternoon Friday, with a drier and chilly evening behind the departing low. A weaker weekend front may bring light, scattered rain late Saturday into Sunday, but the NWS Sacramento office expects Valley totals to stay near a tenth inch or less. Monday is the best pause. A stronger system is increasingly likely Tuesday–Wednesday, although the amount reaching the Delta remains uncertain. Keep an eye on low-lying roads and official Delta flood advisories as high tides rise next week.

East Sacramento.headline: East Sacramento dries out Friday, then tracks a stronger midweek system
East Sacramento.text: East Sacramento may see a few showers linger into early Friday afternoon, but drier weather should return later in the day. Saturday is mostly quiet at first, with a weaker system bringing light Valley rain late Saturday into Sunday; the NWS Sacramento forecast keeps Valley amounts around a tenth inch or less. Monday should be dry. Confidence is increasing in a stronger Tuesday–Wednesday system, with a 50–70% chance of at least an inch across the Sacramento Valley. Mountain travel may also be affected by renewed Sierra snow.
